title: Naturality after fixing residue homology equivalences
statement: In the geometric setup, including an empty family, there exist compatible source and target additive residue homology comparisons and derived arrows satisfying the geometric cohomology pullback equation for every chain representative. The source comparison is chosen once for the entire family; the target comparisons and arrows are chosen with it.

source.place: Tags 0B91, 0BF2, 01XK; parent steps 1, 2 and 4 on homology rather than cycles

proof.text: For n=0 obtain the source comparison from the source geometric comparison theorem and eliminate Fin 0 for the remaining data and equations. For n>0 use the compatible positive-family theorem.

statement_change.old_statement: Given additive equivalences eK and eC as in the geometric comparison, there exist derived arrows a satisfying the induced homology naturality equation for every chain representative.
statement_change.what: The fixed-equivalence helpers universally prescribed arbitrary additive equivalences. Take a smooth plane cubic over C, S=W=Spec(C), k=id, L=O, n=1, Xi=X and ui=id. A strictly perfect model has one-dimensional degree-one residue homology. Choose the source comparison linearly and the target comparison by composing it with complex conjugation in a coordinate. The identity geometric pullback would force conj(H(phi)(z))=z. Every derived arrow between these affine perfect models has a chain representative (perfect_affine_map_representative), and its residue homology map is C-linear, so this is impossible. Instead choose the comparisons together, with one source comparison shared by all indices. The upper geometric naturality theorem already has precisely this existential quantification, and its statement is unchanged.
